read_file.description: Read the contents of a text file from the workspace. Output includes line numbers in the format `LINE_NUMBER|LINE_CONTENT` (1-indexed). Supports partial reads via `start_line` and `length` for large files.

path.description: Path to the file to read. Must start with #cwd/ (workspace root shortcut), e.g. #cwd/memory/MEMORY.md. Absolute paths also allowed.

start_line.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed, inclusive).

length.description: Maximum number of lines to read (default: 200, max: 2000).

write_file.description: Write content to a file, replacing any existing content when overwrite is set. Content is written byte-for-byte after argument decoding. Standard JSON escaping applies: \n for newline and \\n for a literal backslash-n. If the file already exists you must set overwrite=true, which replaces the ENTIRE file.

path.description: Path to the file to write. Must start with #cwd/ (workspace root shortcut), e.g. #cwd/memory/MEMORY.md. Absolute paths also allowed.

content.description: Content to write to the file. Standard JSON escaping applies: \n for newline and \\n for a literal backslash-n.

overwrite.description: Set to true to replace an existing file in full. This discards the file's current contents.

list_dir.description: List files and directories in a folder.

path.description: Path to the folder to list. Must start with #cwd/ (workspace root shortcut), e.g. #cwd/memory/MEMORY.md. Absolute paths also allowed.

grep.description: Search file contents for a keyword across the workspace. Can be narrowed to a single file/folder and a file extension, and limited to a maximum number of matches.

path.description: File or folder to search. Must start with #cwd/ (workspace root shortcut), e.g. #cwd/memory/MEMORY.md. Absolute paths also allowed.

keyword.description: The text to find in file contents.

ext.description: Only search files with this extension (e.g. txt). Empty means all files.

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 50, max: 200).

edit_file.description: Edit a file by replacing old_string with new_string. The old_string must exist exactly once in the file. Standard JSON escaping applies: \n for newline and \\n for a literal backslash-n.

path.description: Path to the file to edit. Must start with #cwd/ (workspace root shortcut), e.g. #cwd/memory/MEMORY.md. Absolute paths also allowed.

old_string.description: The exact text to find and replace. Standard JSON escaping applies: \n for newline and \\n for a literal backslash-n.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with. Standard JSON escaping applies: \n for newline and \\n for a literal backslash-n. Empty string deletes the match.

append_file.description: Append content to the end of a file. Standard JSON escaping applies: \n for newline and \\n for a literal backslash-n.

path.description: Path to the file to append to. Must start with #cwd/ (workspace root shortcut), e.g. #cwd/memory/MEMORY.md. Absolute paths also allowed.

content.description: Content to append to the end of the file. Standard JSON escaping applies: \n for newline and \\n for a literal backslash-n.

run_shell_command.description: Execute shell commands in the workspace. Use background=true for long-running commands (returns a sessionId). Use poll/read/kill with the sessionId to manage background sessions.

action.description: Action to perform: run (execute command), list (show sessions), poll (check status), read (get output), kill (terminate).

command.description: Shell command to execute (required for run).

sessionId.description: Session ID returned by a background run (required for poll/read/kill).

cwd.description: Working directory for the command. Defaults to the workspace root. Must start with #cwd/ or be an absolute path.

telegram_sendfile.description: Send a local file (image, document, etc.) to the user on the current Telegram chat.

path.description: Path to the local file to send. Must start with #cwd/ (workspace root shortcut), e.g. #cwd/memory/MEMORY.md. Absolute paths also allowed.

filename.description: Optional display filename. Defaults to the base name of path.

caption.description: Optional caption shown under the file.

telegram_getuser.description: Look up Telegram user info (name, username, id, bio) for a given user ID.

user_id.description: User ID to look up. Omit to get the current sender.

get_env.description: Get runtime environment info such as workspace path, platform, model, and current date/time.

web_fetch.description: Fetch a URL and extract readable content (HTML to text). Use this to get weather info, news, articles, or any web content. Only public http/https URLs are allowed.

url.description: URL to fetch. Must be a public http/https URL.

section.description: Which representation to return: text (HTML stripped to plain text) or html (raw HTML).

start_line.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed, inclusive).

length.description: Maximum number of lines to return (default: 100, max: 1000).

web_search.description: Search the web for current information. Returns titles, URLs, and snippets from search results.

manage_schedule.description:
Schedule, inspect, and update reminders, tasks, or agent prompts.
IMPORTANT: When the user asks to be reminded or to schedule something, you MUST call this tool.
Use type 'once' with run_once_at for one-time reminders, 'every' with every_seconds ONLY for recurring tasks, 'daily' with daily_time for daily schedules, and 'cron' with cron_expr for complex schedules.

action.description: Action to perform: add, list, get, update, remove, enable, disable. Use 'get' before editing and 'update' to change an existing job without losing its payload.

name.description: Optional job display name for add or update.

prompt.description: The instruction the agent should execute when the job triggers.

type.description: Schedule type: once, every, daily, cron.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for daily or cron schedules (e.g. Asia/Jakarta).

run_once_at.description: When a one-time job should run (for type 'once'). Example: 18:00.

every_seconds.description: Recurring interval in seconds (e.g. 3600 for every hour). Use ONLY for recurring tasks.

weekdays.description: Days of the week the job runs (e.g. ["mon","fri"]). Omit to run every day.

cron_expr.description: Cron expression with 5 fields for complex schedules (e.g. '0 6 * * *' for daily at 06:00).

end_at.description: Optional stop time after which the job no longer runs (e.g. 2026-10-05 00:00).

days.description: Optional number of days the job stays active. 0 means no end.

max_runs.description: Maximum number of runs. 0 means unlimited.

spawn_agent.description: Spawn a sub-agent to handle a specific, self-contained task independently and return its result. The sub-agent runs with its own system prompt and a restricted set of tools granted via the agent_* flags.

system_prompt.description: The sub-agent's role and rules (e.g. "You are a researcher. Return 3 bullets.").

task_prompt.description: The task for the sub-agent to complete.

agent_read.description: Grant the sub-agent read-only file tools.

agent_write.description: Grant the sub-agent file write tools.

agent_exec.description: Grant the sub-agent shell execution tools.

agent_search.description: Grant the sub-agent web search tools.

use_skill.description: Activate a skill by name so its instructions are loaded into the active skills section of the prompt.

name.description: Name of the skill to activate.

always_active.description: Keep the skill active across turns. Defaults to false: the skill lasts for the current turn only and is deactivated after the final answer.

name.description: Name of the skill to deactivate.
